scenes.title: Two Baskets and a List
scenes.summary: After M1 restores kitchen power, F1 and F2 grab woven baskets to shop at the Saturday neighbourhood market while M1 rewires Room 9.
scenes.intro: Twenty minutes after the fuse pop at {SHOW}, kitchen power is back on and {M1} is measuring copper wire in the courtyard. {F1} and {F2} step out into the bright Saturday air with two market baskets. Listen first.
story: The oven is hot again! You saved my Saturday bread, {M1}.
Just keep {M2}'s fingers away from every wall switch until evening.
While you rewire Room Nine, {F2} and I are walking to the Saturday market.
Do you have a written list, or are you buying half the square?
Right here on paper, {M1}: twelve white cups, fresh lemons, and local honey.
Plus four jars of sweet jam and green herbs for our courtyard pots!
Good. Pick up one roll of black tape from the hardware stall too.
One roll of black electrical tape—written down in pencil!
Now you are learning, {F1}. Take the small cash pouch from the desk.
Come on, {F1}, before the best yellow lemons disappear!
Do we need extra chairs at the market, {M1}?
{M2} said he is ordering six folding chairs by phone—wish us luck.
scenes.outro: Baskets in hand and black tape added in pencil, {F1} and {F2} head for the Saturday market—while {M2} makes a phone order unsupervised. See you next time.

scenes.title: Sweet Lemons and Golden Honey
scenes.summary: At the bustling Saturday market, F2 teaches F1 how to choose fragrant lemons and honey when M4 spots them and helps carry the heavy jars.
scenes.intro: Two blocks down {STREET}, colourful canvas stalls fill the Saturday market square. {F1} and {F2} stop beside a fragrant pile of fresh fruit just as {M4} walks past with a paper bag of cherries. Let's listen in first.
story: Smell the skin of this lemon, {F1}—like sunshine after rain!
How many kilos do we need for Friday's tarts and hot tea?
Three kilos of lemons and two big glass jars of flower honey.
Good morning! Need an extra pair of arms for those heavy jars?
{M4}! You found the neighbourhood market already!
I grew up three streets from this square—nothing smells better on Saturday.
Taste a spoon of this dark mountain honey, {M4}. Is it too sweet?
Not at all—warm and rich, just like my mother bought in autumn.
Two big jars and three kilos of lemons, paid in cash with coins to spare!
Give me the heavy basket with the glass jars; you take the herbs.
Next stop: the pottery table at the corner for twelve white teacups!
Lead the way, {F2}—we are ahead of budget already!
scenes.outro: Three kilos of fragrant lemons and two heavy jars of honey are safely in {M4}'s basket. See you at the pottery stall next time.

scenes.title: Twelve White Cups
scenes.summary: M3 meets the group at the market pottery stall and helps F1 and F2 choose thick white stoneware cups that keep tea hot.
scenes.intro: At the sunny corner of the market square, {M3} is sketching an arched stone doorway when {F1} and {F2} arrive at the ceramic table. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: Look at all these cups, {F2}: tall blue mugs, thin glass cups, round white bowls!
Thin cups look pretty, {F1}, but tea goes cold in three minutes.
Try the thick cream-white stoneware on the left shelf.
Oh, hello, {M3}! Your brother is right behind us holding the honey.
Feel the handle on this cup—thick clay holds heat and never chips easily.
And listen to that soft clink when you set it on the saucer!
Quiet saucers mean guests can hear {F3}'s piano across the room.
Even when buying teacups, {M3} thinks like an acoustic architect!
If we buy twelve cups and twelve saucers together, is there a discount?
Look at the chalk sign: ten percent off a full dozen!
Plus a matching white milk jug on the side—wrap them in newspaper.
Packed and paid! Don't forget {M1}'s black tape on the way home!
scenes.outro: Twelve thick stoneware cups, quiet saucers, and a matching milk jug are wrapped in paper—with {M1}'s black tape remembered too. See you next time.

scenes.title: Thursday Means Today?
scenes.summary: Back at the inn, M2 proudly tells M1 about the bargain café chairs he ordered—then realises he said 'Saturday' instead of 'Thursday'.
scenes.intro: Back at {SHOW}, {M1} is stripping clean copper wire on a stool when {M2} strolls up to the front desk beaming with pride over his telephone bargain. Listen first.
story: Congratulate me, {M1}! I found folding wooden garden chairs at half price!
Half price? Why do I already feel nervous when you say 'half price'?
Because the shop only gives that price if you order two dozen at once!
Two dozen?! {M2}, two dozen is twenty-four chairs!
Twelve for Room Nine, eight spares for the courtyard, and four for... emergencies!
Where on earth do we store twenty-four chairs while we paint all week?!
Relax! I told the driver to bring them next Thursday afternoon.
Wait—who just backed a delivery van up to our front gate?
A blue van? Why does the side say 'Garden Chairs Express'?!
Let me read your notepad... boss, you circled 'Saturday two o'clock'!
I read the wrong column without my glasses! They are unloading them now!
Twenty-four wooden chairs in our narrow courtyard—wonderful, boss!
scenes.outro: Without his glasses, {M2} ordered twenty-four chairs for Saturday afternoon instead of Thursday, and the delivery van is already at the gate! See you next time.

scenes.title: A Mountain of Chairs
scenes.summary: F1 and F2 return from the market to find M2 trapped behind towers of unpainted folding chairs blocking the courtyard path.
scenes.intro: Carrying wrapped cups and market baskets, {F1} and {F2} push open the courtyard gate—and stop dead in front of {M2}, who is surrounded by tall stacks of wooden chairs. Let's listen in first.
story: {M2}?! Where did all these wooden chairs come from?!
There is a wall of chairs from the lemon pot all the way to the stairs!
Good news first: every single chair was fifty percent off!
And what is the bad news, {M2}?
I asked for six, agreed to twenty-four, and accidentally said 'today'!
How will our upstairs guests walk to the street without climbing over wood?!
Wait—look how flat each chair folds when you press the side latch!
Oh! Four folded chairs take no more space than one suitcase!
Lift the seat slightly, fold it flat, and lean twelve neatly under the dry arch.
And put twelve straight into Room Nine once {M1} finishes the lamp!
{F1}, promoting you to permanent receptionist saved my life twice in two days!
scenes.outro: Folding the chairs flat clears the courtyard path in minutes and turns {M2}'s mistake into neat stacks under the arch. See you next time.

scenes.title: Light in Room Nine
scenes.summary: Using the black tape from the market, M1 finishes the new copper wiring and switches on the warm glass ceiling lamp in Room 9.
scenes.intro: Inside Room 9, {M1} wraps the last joint with the new roll of black tape while {F1} holds the stepladder and {M3} checks the wall socket. Listen first.
story: Hand me the small brass screws from your pocket, {F1}.
One, two. Is the new copper wire connected all the way to the box?
Brand-new wire, new porcelain fuse, and zero old cloth left in the wall.
The brass switch plate sits straight and tight against the brick.
Step down clear of the ladder. Ready to test it properly, {F1}?
Should we call {M2} to flip the switch?
Not a chance. Your turn, {F1}—one clean click.
Here goes... click! Oh, look at that warm golden light!
The frosted glass shade spreads soft light across every windowpane!
Listen to the kitchen too—no pop, and the oven is still humming.
Room Nine officially has light after thirty dark years!
Wait—look at the shadow inside the open piano lid, {F1}!
scenes.outro: The frosted ceiling lamp glows warm gold without tripping a single fuse—and its light reveals something tucked inside the piano lid! See you next time.

scenes.title: Inside the Piano Lid
scenes.summary: Under the new ceiling lamp, F3, F1, and M3 pull a folded sheet of handwritten piano music from behind the wooden music rest.
scenes.intro: {F1} calls {F3} into the newly lit sunroom, where {M3} points to a cream paper corner wedged behind the piano's wooden music stand. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: You fixed the ceiling lamp! The walnut wood shines like honey now!
Look right here behind the folding music desk when the lamp shines down.
Is that folded music paper stuck inside the hinge?
Let me slide it out gently with two fingers so the paper does not tear.
Handwritten notes in black ink! Can you read the title on top, {F3}?
'Courtyard Waltz — for Friday Evening Tea, May, thirty years ago.'
That matches the exact date on the postcard in the cedar box!
Let me hum the opening bar... oh, what a gentle, singing melody!
Wait—turn the sheet over! Half of page two is blank!
The composer wrote twenty-four bars and stopped right in the middle of a phrase!
And look at the pencilled note at the bottom: 'Finish before Friday.'
Why did the music stop thirty years ago—and who wrote it?!
scenes.outro: Hidden inside the piano sits an unfinished handwritten 'Courtyard Waltz' from thirty years ago! One final scene for Episode 2—let's listen.

scenes.title: Ask My Aunt's Ledger
scenes.summary: F3 shows M2 the unfinished handwritten waltz, and M2 recognises his late aunt's handwriting—right as the city clerk leaves an urgent message.
scenes.intro: At the front desk as Saturday evening settles in, {F1} and {F3} lay the handwritten sheet of music under the desk lamp in front of {M2}. Listen first.
story: {M2}, look what was hiding inside the upright piano in Room Nine!
Handwritten music? Let me pull my glasses down... wait a second!
Do you know who wrote 'Courtyard Waltz' thirty years ago, {M2}?
Look at those round capital letters—that is my aunt's handwriting!
Your aunt played the piano and ran the Friday tea room?!
She baked cakes in the morning and wrote little songs at night!
Why did she stop halfway through page two in May thirty years ago?
Her old green guest book from that spring is still in the attic chest!
Wait—the front desk telephone is blinking with a recorded voice message.
Press play, {F1}! Who calls on Saturday evening?!
It is the city heritage office... they moved our café inspection to Wednesday at three!
Wednesday at three?! That gives us three days instead of six!
scenes.outro: The unfinished waltz belonged to {M2}'s aunt—and the city heritage visit just jumped forward from Friday to Wednesday at three! Episode 2 is complete—see you in Episode 3.
